22PRr1::22PRr1_2531955_3: This dark family is associated with predicted surface-filament proteins in 13 verified loci spanning six genus blocks. Ten partners belong to F37Dr2::F37Dr2_752038_3 and three to S20PRr1::S20PRr1_1478121_8; their catalogue annotations link PF04964 to PilJ-like or archaellum-related reference proteins. Every pair is immediately adjacent and co-oriented, with signed intergenic gaps from -4 to 37 bp. This supports a conserved local gene-module hypothesis. The primary context association passes the joint correction, but the genus-restricted sensitivity does not; these are not independent confirmations. The complete interior representative is predicted to be membrane anchored. Verified structural models are available only for a contig-edge seed member, and no complete interior member has a verified model. Consequently, the current structural evidence cannot establish or exclude a function for the complete protein. Co-transcription, archaeal pilin identity, adhesion, motility and biochemical activity remain unestablished.
V60PRr2::V60PRr2_1314979_4: This dark family is associated with predicted S-layer-related proteins in 11 verified loci spanning five genus blocks. The partners belong to three annotated families, with six, three and two loci respectively. Every pair is immediately adjacent and co-oriented, with signed intergenic gaps from -4 to 6 bp. This supports a conserved local gene-module hypothesis involving a predicted exported dark protein and a predicted surface protein. The primary context association passes the joint correction, but the genus-restricted sensitivity does not. An exact sequence-matched structural model is available for a contig-edge seed member; no complete interior member has a verified model. That model does not establish a role for the complete protein, and limited reference-panel results must not be interpreted as absence of homology. Co-transcription, S-layer membership, substrate specificity and biochemical activity remain unestablished.
